doc.calendar_a11y_1: Navigate through dates using keyboard arrow keys.
doc.calendar_a11y_2: Select a date using Enter or Space keys.
doc.calendar_a11y_3: Change months using Page Up and Page Down keys.
doc.calendar_a11y_4: Compliant with WAI-ARIA calendar design patterns.
doc.calendar_a11y_5: Selected and disabled states are communicated via aria-selected and aria-disabled.
doc.calendar_behavior_1: Select the start date on the first click.
doc.calendar_behavior_2: Select the end date on the second click.
doc.calendar_behavior_3: The range between start and end dates is highlighted during selection.
doc.calendar_behavior_4: If a date before the start date is selected as the end date, they are automatically swapped.
doc.calendar_controlled_uncontrolled_desc: The Calendar component supports both controlled and uncontrolled patterns.
doc.calendar_disabled_by_function_desc: By passing a function to isDateDisabled, you can flexibly disable dates based on conditions like weekends or past dates.
doc.calendar_disabled_dates_desc: There are two ways to disable dates: by passing an array or a function.
doc.calendar_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through locale-aware date formatting and the aria-label props.
doc.calendar_integration_datepicker_desc: Calendar is used as an internal component of DatePicker. Use this component directly for standalone calendar needs.
doc.calendar_keyboard_desc: Arrow keys navigate between dates. Page Up and Page Down move between months. Home and End move to the first and last day of the month. Enter or Space selects the focused date.
doc.calendar_long_desc: Details and usage for the Calendar component.
doc.calendar_min_max_dates_desc: Limit the selectable range with minDate and maxDate properties. Dates outside this range will be grayed out.
doc.calendar_range_mode_desc: Enable starting and ending date range selection by setting the rangeMode property.
doc.calendar_week_start_desc: Use the `weekStartsOn` prop to set the first day of the week. `0` starts on Sunday (default), `1` starts on Monday.
doc.datagrid_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.datagrid_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.datagrid_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.datagrid_best_practice_1: Use DataGrid consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.datagrid_best_practice_2: Test DataGrid behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.datagrid_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Table better suits the use case.
doc.datagrid_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.datagrid_choice_self_when: When DataGrid functionality with standard options is required.
doc.datagrid_content_guideline: Keep content concise and relevant to the component's purpose. Follow consistent labeling conventions across your application.
doc.datagrid_design_intent: DataGrid provides a consistent, reusable pattern for advanced data table with sorting, selection, and pagination, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.datagrid_infinite_scroll_desc: Use the loadMore prop to fetch additional rows as the user scrolls down. An alternative to pagination for large, continuously growing datasets such as logs or activity feeds.
doc.datagrid_motion_desc: Transitions are minimal and purposeful, respecting the user's reduced-motion preferences.
doc.datagrid_right_fixed_col_desc: Set fixed="right" on a column to pin it to the right edge of the grid. Useful for action columns that must remain visible during horizontal scrolling.
doc.datagrid_scenario_1: Admin Dashboard: Display user lists, order management, and product catalogs combining sorting, row selection, and pagination for efficient data browsing.
doc.datagrid_scenario_2: Report & Analytics: Browse large datasets with sticky headers and fixed columns. Combine with CSV export for offline analysis.
doc.datagrid_scenario_3: Infinite Scroll Feed: Use loadMore to append rows on scroll, providing a seamless experience for large log tables or activity feeds without page breaks.
doc.ganttchart_a11y_desc: Keyboard support and ARIA roles for navigating between tasks and interacting with the timeline.
doc.ganttchart_a11y_key_arrow_down: Focus the next task in the list.
doc.ganttchart_a11y_key_arrow_up: Focus the previous task in the list.
doc.ganttchart_a11y_key_enter: Select or trigger the click handler for the focused task.
doc.ganttchart_a11y_key_tab: Move focus between the chart and other interactive elements.
doc.ganttchart_anatomy_bar: The horizontal bar representing the total duration of a task.
doc.ganttchart_anatomy_header: The top row displaying the timeline scale (weeks/months).
doc.ganttchart_anatomy_label_panel: The left panel containing task names and labels.
doc.ganttchart_anatomy_progress: The inner portion of the task bar indicating its completion percentage.
doc.ganttchart_best_practice_1: Avoid overcrowding the timeline with too many tasks; use filtering or pagination if necessary.
doc.ganttchart_best_practice_2: Provide tooltips for task bars to show detailed start/end dates and progress.
doc.ganttchart_best_practice_3: Sync the scroll between the label panel and the timeline for a seamless experience.
doc.ganttchart_choice_alt_kanban_when: When the goal is to manage task status and workflow stages rather than precise timing.
doc.ganttchart_choice_alt_table_when: When the focus is on metadata and sorting rather than visual timeline representation.
doc.ganttchart_choice_alt_timeline_when: When you want to show a simple vertical history of events rather than task durations.
doc.ganttchart_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on the complexity and type of chronological information.
doc.ganttchart_choice_self_when: When you need to visualize project schedules, task durations, and overlapping activities over a specific timeline.
doc.ganttchart_content_guideline_1: Keep task labels concise to ensure readability in the label panel.
doc.ganttchart_content_guideline_2: Ensure task dates are valid to avoid rendering errors on the timeline.
doc.ganttchart_content_guideline_3: Group related tasks or use consistent colors to distinguish between different project phases.
doc.ganttchart_design_intent: To provide a highly readable and interactive way to visualize project timelines, dependencies, and progress, helping users manage complex schedules efficiently.
doc.ganttchart_i18n_desc: Supports localized date formats and RTL layouts.
doc.ganttchart_keyboard_desc: Full keyboard navigation support for accessibility compliance.
doc.ganttchart_long_desc: A Gantt chart is a bar chart that illustrates a project schedule. This component displays tasks, durations, and progress in a clear, timeline-based format.
doc.ganttchart_motion_desc: Smooth transitions when changing views or updating data, with subtle hover states for task bars.
doc.ganttchart_responsive_desc: On mobile, the label panel may be sticky or reduced to icons to maximize timeline visibility.
doc.ganttchart_scenario_project_desc: Mapping out product development cycles and team milestones.
doc.ganttchart_scenario_release_desc: Visualizing deployment phases and QA windows for a software release.
doc.ganttchart_token_bg: The background color of the label panel and timeline.
doc.ganttchart_token_border: Used for grid lines and separators.
doc.ganttchart_token_duration: Controls the speed of transitions when switching views.
doc.ganttchart_token_font: Smaller font size for timeline labels to save space.
doc.ganttchart_token_primary: Used for the task bar and progress indicator.
doc.ganttchart_token_text: The color of task labels and header dates.
doc.ganttchart_visual_guideline_progress: The progress bar should have enough contrast against the background task bar. Usually, a darker shade of the primary color is used for the completed portion.
doc.kanban_a11y_desc: KanbanBoard uses role="region". Cards use role="listitem" with aria-disabled for disabled state. Column titles serve as accessible labels for each drop zone.
doc.kanban_anatomy_board: The root container that provides drag-and-drop context and holds all columns in a horizontal layout.
doc.kanban_anatomy_card: A draggable item within a column. Becomes non-draggable when disabled.
doc.kanban_anatomy_column: A vertical lane with a header (title + card count badge) and a body that acts as a drop target.
doc.kanban_best_practice_1: Keep column count to 3–6 for readability. Too many columns make it hard to see the overall workflow.
doc.kanban_best_practice_2: Card data and column assignment should be managed in parent state. Use the onCardMove callback to update state and re-render.
doc.kanban_best_practice_3: Use the disabled prop on cards that should not be moved — for example, cards that are locked by another user or in a finalized state.
doc.kanban_choice_alt_list_when: When tasks do not have stage-based progression and a simple ordered list is sufficient.
doc.kanban_choice_alt_table_when: When tasks need to be displayed in a sortable tabular format with multiple columns of metadata.
doc.kanban_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.kanban_choice_self_when: When visualizing work items that progress through distinct stages (e.g. To Do → In Progress → Done) and drag-and-drop reordering is needed.
doc.kanban_content_guideline_1: Keep card content concise — a title and optionally a short description or label is ideal.
doc.kanban_content_guideline_2: Use the cardCount prop on columns to show the number of items at a glance.
doc.kanban_desc: Drag-and-drop board for visualizing workflow stages
doc.kanban_design_intent: Kanban provides a visual way to manage work items across stages using a drag-and-drop interface. State ownership remains with the parent, keeping the component flexible for any workflow.
doc.kanban_disabled_card_desc: Cards with the disabled prop cannot be dragged and are visually dimmed.
doc.kanban_i18n_desc: Supports labels for different column states like Todo, Doing, Done.
doc.kanban_keyboard_desc: Cards can be moved between columns using keyboard shortcuts.
doc.kanban_long_desc: A compound component for building Kanban boards with draggable cards across customizable columns.
doc.kanban_motion_desc: Drag-over columns are highlighted with a subtle border and background change. Dragging cards fade to indicate the source position.
doc.kanban_responsive_desc: Adapts to mobile by stacking columns or using a tab view.
doc.kanban_scenario_1: Tracking feature requests or bug reports across stages: Reported → Triaged → In Progress → Resolved.
doc.kanban_scenario_2: Managing sprint tasks across columns: Backlog → In Progress → Review → Done.
doc.kanban_token_radius: Border radius of cards and columns.
doc.kanban_token_shadow: Shadow applied to cards during drag.
doc.table_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.table_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.table_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.table_basic_desc: This is the simplest table configuration.
doc.table_best_practice_1: Use Table consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.table_best_practice_2: Test Table behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.table_bordered_desc: With the `bordered` prop, borders are displayed around the entire table and each cell.
doc.table_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like DataGrid better suits the use case.
doc.table_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.table_choice_self_when: When Table functionality with standard options is required.
doc.table_compound_desc: The `Table` is composed of the following sub-components:
doc.table_content_guideline: Keep content concise and relevant to the component's purpose. Follow consistent labeling conventions across your application.
doc.table_desc: Rows and columns for displaying structured data efficiently
doc.table_design_intent: Table provides a consistent, reusable pattern for structured data display in rows and columns, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.table_fullwidth_desc: The `fullWidth` prop makes the table expand to the full width of its parent container.
doc.table_hoverable_desc: The `hoverable` prop highlights the row under the mouse cursor.
doc.table_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through column header and cell content props.
doc.table_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through sortable column headers and interactive cells. Arrow keys navigate between cells where applicable.
doc.table_long_desc: The table component is used to display organized data.
doc.table_motion_desc: Transitions are minimal and purposeful, respecting the user's reduced-motion preferences.
doc.table_row_selection_desc: A feature to select multiple rows using checkboxes. You can style the column by passing `selection` to `Table.Head` and `Table.Cell`.
doc.table_scenario_1: Data Inventory: Managing thousands of product rows with sorting and multi-selection capabilities.
doc.table_scenario_2: Financial History: Displaying transaction records with clear column headers and striped row styling.
doc.table_scrollbar_desc: The appearance of the scrollbar can be adjusted using the `scrollbar` prop.
doc.table_sort_manual_desc: You can also implement your own sorting logic without the hook.
doc.table_sortable_desc: A sorting UI can be displayed by passing the `sortable` prop to `Table.Head` elements.
doc.table_striped_desc: Using the `striped` prop colors the rows alternately.
doc.table_title: Rows and columns for displaying structured data efficiently
doc.table_ts_support_desc: The Table component and useTableSort hook provide complete type definitions.
doc.table_usetablesort_desc: The Table component provides a `useTableSort` hook to easily implement sorting functionality.
doc.table_usetablesort_feature_custom: Customizable: Supports initial sort state and onChange callbacks
doc.table_usetablesort_feature_logic: Auto sort logic: Appropriately handles strings, numbers, and null values
doc.table_with_actions_desc: It is possible to place interactive elements like buttons inside cells.
doc.treeview_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.treeview_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.treeview_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.treeview_api_item_icon: Icon displayed on the left of the label.
doc.treeview_api_oncheckedchange: Callback triggered when the checked state changes.
doc.treeview_api_width: The width of the container. Animates upon changing.
doc.treeview_best_practice_1: Use TreeView consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.treeview_best_practice_2: Test TreeView behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.treeview_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like List better suits the use case.
doc.treeview_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.treeview_choice_self_when: When TreeView functionality with standard options is required.
doc.treeview_content_guideline: Keep content concise and relevant to the component's purpose. Follow consistent labeling conventions across your application.
doc.treeview_custom_icons_desc: Custom icons can be set for each item.
doc.treeview_design_intent: TreeView provides a consistent, reusable pattern for expandable hierarchical tree display for navigating nested data, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.treeview_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through the label prop of each TreeView.Item.
doc.treeview_keyboard_desc: Arrow keys navigate the tree hierarchy. Right arrow expands a node; Left arrow collapses it or moves to parent. Enter or Space selects an item.
doc.treeview_long_desc: The `TreeView` component is used to display hierarchical data. It is ideal for displaying file systems, organizational charts, and category hierarchies.
doc.treeview_motion_desc: Transitions are minimal and purposeful, respecting the user's reduced-motion preferences.
doc.treeview_multi_select_desc: Using the `multiSelect` property allows you to select multiple items at once.
doc.treeview_overflow_desc: The TreeView component is designed to maintain a consistent width (100% by default) to avoid layout shifts. When labels are too long, they are automatically truncated with an ellipsis (...).
doc.treeview_scenario_1: File Browsing: Navigating nested directory structures with folder expansion and file selection.
doc.treeview_scenario_2: Permission Hierarchy: Visualizing and managing access levels across an organizational chart.
doc.treeview_search_filter_desc: When the `searchable` property is enabled, an input field is displayed allowing you to search for items within the tree.
doc.treeview_search_filter_note: When searching, only matching items and their parent items are displayed.
doc.treeview_title: An interactive display for data organized in a tree or nested hierarchy
doc.treeview_ts_support_desc: The TreeView components support full type environments.
doc.nodegraph_desc: A component for rendering interactive node-based diagrams. Built on React Flow, it is used for visualizing and editing complex graph structures like approval flows and AI pipelines.
doc.nodegraph_design_intent: Designed for visual exploration and editing of directed graphs. Supports node dragging, connection creation, and read-only modes.
doc.nodegraph_anatomy_root: The main interactive area where nodes and edges are rendered.
doc.nodegraph_anatomy_node: Interactive elements representing entities or process steps.
doc.nodegraph_anatomy_edge: Visual connections representing relationships or flow between nodes.
doc.nodegraph_content_label: Keep node labels short and concise (e.g., 'Approve', 'Send', 'Condition').
doc.nodegraph_content_edge: Describe state transition conditions on edge labels (e.g., 'success', 'error').
doc.nodegraph_motion_drag: Node dragging uses native browser behavior. Default React Flow animations are maintained.
doc.nodegraph_a11y_wrap: The entire graph is wrapped in role="region" with an aria-label.
doc.nodegraph_a11y_keyboard: Keyboard navigation for node selection and movement depends on React Flow's built-in support.
doc.nodegraph_a11y_live: We recommend announcing important state changes via a separate aria-live region.
doc.nodegraph_scenario_flow_desc: Building workflows by connecting nodes for requests, approvals, and rejections.
doc.nodegraph_scenario_ai_desc: Visualizing processing flows like Prompt -> LLM -> Post-processing.
doc.nodegraph_scenario_data_desc: Mapping ETL pipelines and API integration dependencies.
doc.nodegraph_best_init: Pass initial nodes and edges via nodes/edges props; React Flow manages internal state.
doc.nodegraph_best_readonly: Combine nodesDraggable={false}, nodesConnectable={false}, and deleteKeyCode={null} for a read-only view.
doc.nodegraph_best_height: Always specify an explicit height for the container (e.g., 500px); the graph won't render if height is 0.
doc.nodegraph_responsive_desc: Resizes automatically to container width and height. Consider disabling controls on mobile to avoid small touch targets.
doc.nodegraph_keyboard_undo: Undo (requires custom implementation on the consumer side)
doc.nodegraph_i18n_desc: The component itself has no translation keys; localize node and edge labels in the provided data.
doc.scheduleview_desc: A calendar (TimeGrid) component with a time axis. Built on FullCalendar, it supports switching between week, day, and month views, drag-and-drop events, and creating appointments by selecting time slots.
doc.scheduleview_design_intent: Provides an intuitive schedule management UI like Google Calendar. Supports not only viewing but also moving/resizing events via drag-and-drop and creating new ones by clicking empty slots.
doc.scheduleview_anatomy_root: The calendar container that coordinates views and time slots.
doc.scheduleview_anatomy_event: Interactive blocks representing scheduled tasks or appointments.
doc.scheduleview_anatomy_toolbar: Controls for switching views and navigating time periods.
doc.scheduleview_content_title: Keep event titles short (under 15 chars) for better visibility in the time grid.
doc.scheduleview_content_color: Recommend using color-coding to distinguish between categories, assignees, or priorities.
doc.scheduleview_motion_drag: Uses FullCalendar's default animations. A mirror element is displayed during dragging to provide visual feedback.
doc.scheduleview_a11y_wrap: The entire calendar is wrapped in role="region" with an aria-label.
doc.scheduleview_a11y_keyboard: Keyboard event interaction (moving via arrow keys) is handled by the browser and FullCalendar.
doc.scheduleview_scenario_shift_desc: Dragging and dropping staff shifts on the weekly time grid.
doc.scheduleview_scenario_booking_desc: Clicking empty slots to create bookings and prevent double-booking.
doc.scheduleview_scenario_project_desc: Overviewing milestones and deadlines in the monthly view.
doc.scheduleview_best_height: Provide an explicit height for the container (e.g., 600px); height="100%" depends on the parent element's height.
doc.scheduleview_best_slots: Limit business hours with slotMinTime/slotMaxTime to reduce scrolling.
doc.scheduleview_best_dialog: Implement onDateSelect to integrate with a dialog for entering appointment details.
doc.scheduleview_responsive_desc: Resizes automatically to container width. Recommend switching to day view (initialView="timeGridDay") on mobile.
doc.scheduleview_i18n_desc: Passing "ja" or "pt" to the locale prop automatically localizes days and months. FullCalendar locale data is loaded automatically.
